issues.issue: Does the statutory bar in s.72(2)(e) IRPA cover the reconsideration order and the costs award?
issues.applicant_position: Says the costs award against counsel is separate from immigration matters, so it escapes the statutory appeal bar.
issues.respondent_position: Submits the notice of appeal should be removed and the file closed because the statutory bar applies.
issues.result_quote: Thus, through and through, this matter falls within the bar against appeals set out in para. 72(2)(e) of the Act.

issues.issue: Does s.27 of the Federal Courts Act give this Court power to hear the appeal despite the bar?
issues.applicant_position: Says s.27 of the Federal Courts Act gives this Court jurisdiction to hear the appeal.
issues.result_quote: I do not accept this submission.

issues.issue: Do constitutional questions or the Federal Court's role on judicial review take the appeal outside the bar?
issues.result_quote: Para. 72(2)(e) is the law of the land; it is no part of our role to fashion an exception that effectively repeals Parliament’s bar.

issues.issue: Can constitutional arguments (s.72 and costs against counsel) be considered on appeal when they were not raised in the Federal Court?
issues.applicant_position: Intends to argue that s.72 and the costs award against counsel personally are unconstitutional.
issues.result_quote: the appellants’ failure to advance their constitutional arguments in the Federal Court disables this Court from considering them.

issues.issue: Should the notice of appeal be removed because it lacks sufficient particularity under the Federal Courts Rules?
issues.respondent_position: Submits the notice of appeal lacks sufficient particularity to qualify as a notice of appeal under the Rules.
issues.result_quote: I also agree with the Minister’s submission that the notice of appeal does not contain sufficient particularity to qualify as a “notice of appeal”

issues.issue: Should costs be awarded against the appellants?
issues.result_quote: There are no special reasons under Rule 22 of the Federal Courts Citizenship, Immigration and Refugee Protection Rules that would warrant an award of costs against the appellants.
